To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
chemokine receptors, CXCR4 and, CCR7 promote breast cancer metastasis by inhibiting anoikis.
the chemokine receptor CXCR4 and its ligand, CXCL12, are important mediators of the anoikis resistance in metastatic breast cancer.

chemokines CXCL12 and its receptor CXCR4 and their counterparts CCL21 and CCR7 are important regulators of anoikis in metastatic breast cancer and that they may offer a new therapeutic target for the treatment of breast and potentially other types of cancers.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanisms of metastatic spread of cancer cells and the development of novel therapeutic strategies for the treatment of breast cancer and other metastatic tumors.

the role of chemokine receptors in the metastatic process and the mechanisms by which these receptors promote tumor cell survival in the circulation and the establishment of secondary tumors in the metastatic cascade.
the role of chemokine receptors in metastasis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
CXCR4 and/or CCR7 are involved in anoikis resistance of breast cancer cells by a novel mechanism of regulating Bmf and Bcl-xL levels.
the chemokine receptor CXCR4 and its ligand CXCL12 promote breast cancer metastasis by preventing detachment-induced cell death or anoikis in breast cancer cells.
the chemokine receptor-mediated regulation of anoikis sensitivity may provide a previously unrecognized axis in malignant tumors which connects chemokines with the metastatic process.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
CXCL12 and its receptor, CXCR4, and CCL21 and its receptor, CCR7, promote metastasis in part by inhibiting anoikis, a detachment-induced form of cell death, in cancer cells.
chemokine receptors, by inhibiting anoikis in breast cancer cells, promote metastasis by allowing the survival of cancer cells that detach from the primary tumor.
the metastatic spread is a multistep process that requires the ability of cancer cells to survive in the absence of appropriate cell – ECM interactions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
chemokine receptors can be used to prevent anoikis and thus metastatic spread in breast cancer.
chemokine receptors are not only involved in the initial steps of metastasis but also in the survival and proliferation of metastatic cells in the distant organs.
CXCR4 and/or CCR7 can be targeted to prevent the spread of metastatic breast tumors to the lungs.
